name: Hannah — 120 thermic hours, careful, never had a collapse, no SIV course
summary: Flies two or three times a month, well past 100 thermic hours, regular 20-30km cross-countries from several different sites. Practises wingovers, spirals and asymmetrics on her own but has never done a manoeuvres course, and has never actually had a collapse. Walks away from days she doesn't like and is comfortable doing it. Can name the flights her current wing cost her.
why_this_persona: The 'cautious but capable' profile the brief asks for, and the main negative control on two mechanisms. First, SIV: she reaches Ready having never done a course, and her total clears the threshold before the bonus is added. Second, collapse history: she has never had a collapse, which scores exactly 0.5 — on the Ready-blocker line, passing by the narrowest margin — and must not drop her a band. If either of those ever changes, this rubric has started requiring an event and a course the sources don't require.

notes: Computed skills 86.7, psychological 98.1, total 92.1, no bonus (manoeuvre_course: no). Clear of the 78 threshold and both category floors (72/68) with real margin, and every critical_check_floor member passes.

The margin matters structurally, not just numerically: she is Ready WITHOUT the 2-point manoeuvres bonus, so no part of this result depends on SIV. 'siv_before_you_upgrade' still fires — twice over, on 'never had a collapse' and on not having done a course — and its body opens by saying it is optional and that the result is unaffected. That pairing is the whole SIV design at this step: strong suggestion, no score.

'collapse_experience: never' scores exactly 0.5, which is the minimum for the Ready-blocker, so it passes rather than being excused. The scoring config marks it down from 0.55 one rung below on the reasoning that 100-plus thermic hours with no collapse is less informative than the same answer from a low-B soaring pilot — this persona is the check that the markdown stopped there and did not become a penalty.
'post_collapse_support' must NOT fire. Its trigger needs a collapse that went wrong or a recent fright; 'never' is neither, and conflating the two would misread her.

'speed_bar_half_bar_routine' fires on 'a bit of bar on most glides', which is full marks' worth of behaviour at A to low-B and 0.8 here. That is the clearest small example of this step's scoring being a band harder on an identical option set.
'descent_toolkit' must NOT fire: she has ears, bigger folds and a practised spiral, which is the top band.

TONE CHECK: she is careful, she declines days, and nothing in a Ready result may read as congratulating her for being willing to push harder. docs/design-context.md's safety guard forbids reassurance as a design goal — her result should read as 'the evidence is there', not as 'go on then'.
